what: Review item R16-R2: checkout writes the whole product row, so a mask does not limit what is written. The catalog says the mask only shapes the read-back and does not limit writes, so the checkout code (or its mask use) is wrong. A concurrent checkout fails with 'no records updated' and surfaces as a 500, not NOT_ENOUGH_STOCK.
heading: ### Platform: the DAO update call
replaces: With a mask, only the fields named in the mask are written ("Pattern 4: Partial Updates" in the [data access guide](../../agent-docs/backend/data-access-guide.md#using-masks-projections)). Without a mask every attribute the payload carries is updated.
proposed: The mask does not limit the write: `update(entity, mask)` writes every attribute the payload carries, and the mask only shapes the read-back ("Pattern 4: Partial Updates" in the [data access guide](../../agent-docs/backend/data-access-guide.md#using-masks-projections)). To write fewer fields, pass a payload that carries only those fields.
evidence: target/judo-ng-read/wt/template__judo-psm-generator-sdk-core/judo-psm-generator-sdk-core-impl/src/main/resources/dao/impl/dao.implementation.java.hbs:327-343 (payload is data.toMap(); the mask goes only into the read-back QueryCustomizer) | catalog/agent-docs/backend/data-access-guide.md:434-436 (Pattern 4 states the rule correctly) | session:L6346 | app:application/app/src/main/java/com/example/webshop/webshop/custom/webshop/StockService.java:18-25,80 (the fixed write carries identifier, version and two attributes)
note: The checkout write was the builder's mistake and the app has since been fixed (StockService writes id, version and two attributes). The catalog Pattern 4 text is correct; the best-practice sentence above is wrong. The rationale bullet at line 53 of the same file ('keeps unrelated fields untouched') repeats the same wrong idea and needs the same correction in the same edit. The 500 on a stale version is documented in platform-behavior-reference.md (Optimistic Locking and __version); no framework defect.

what: Review item R16-R5: ProductAuditInterceptor writes audit rows in preCall and catches RuntimeException (line 79) and continues. On PostgreSQL a failed insert aborts the whole transaction, so the update fails later with a confusing error, and the catalog's note on caught DAO exceptions is not followed.
heading: ### Platform base: what an exception costs you
replaces: A secondary interceptor that must not break the write has to catch its own failures.
proposed: A secondary interceptor that must not break the write has to catch its own failures, except a failed database write: on PostgreSQL a caught DAO failure aborts the whole transaction, so the next statement fails. Let such a failure propagate so the operation rolls back, or move the write to an async interceptor.
evidence: app:application/interceptors/src/main/java/com/example/webshop/interceptors/ProductAuditInterceptor.java:79-80 (catches RuntimeException and continues, citing safe-failure-pattern) | catalog/best-practices/backend/safe-failure-pattern.md:25 | catalog/agent-docs/backend/custom-operations.md (Rules for Custom Operations: a caught DAO exception does not roll back by itself) | session:L6115,L6287,L6293
note: The app code followed the catalog sentence literally (its comment cites safe-failure-pattern), and the sentence is what misleads. The PostgreSQL abort rule itself is already documented in the same file (Platform base) and in custom-operations.md. A grep of judo-runtime-core found no savepoint API for DAO writes, so the proposal does not offer one. Line 79 was taken from the input item and the surrounding code was checked.
